title: Grateful Dead Live at Thelma Theater on 1969-12-12
source: Master Soundboard Reel > Reel to Reel > DAT > CDR

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording that sharpens midway, delivering a late‑1969 set highlighted by an epic Alligator > Caution > Feedback stretch and a haunting Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The tape starts out a bit gritty, but once the mix settles around Lovelight the performance shines. Reviewers rave about the extended Alligator jam flowing into a jazzy Caution and a melodic Feedback, plus standout moments like He Was A Friend of Mine, King Bee with Pigpen’s harp, and a uniquely harmonized Lovelight. The soundboard source is generally well‑balanced with Tom Constanten front‑and‑center, making the later half of the show truly release‑worthy.

ai_rating.rationale: 7 detailed reviews overwhelmingly positive (mostly 5‑star) praise both musical performance and recording quality; only one neutral comment, so the combined show‑recording assessment is very strong.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early part sounds a bit gritty and 'grates', but mid‑set onward the mix clears up; Tom Constanten’s keyboards are prominent, overall balance is solid with clear instrument separation.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first half is uneven, but the second half flows superbly with extended jams and seamless segues, culminating in a powerful closing sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone is praised, especially on Lovelight’s counter‑harmony and the jam sections; noted for strong interplay with Pigpen.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned for ‘bombs’ (bass) during the Alligator jam and overall solid support.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten is heavy in the mix, highlighted as a key element of the performance; his departure a month later adds historic interest.
band_member_comments.Drums: Energetic drum segment within Alligator noted; reviewers wish the drum solo were uninterrupted.
